title: Sierra Halo client intake — integration dossier
content:
TL;DR: Call 2026-03-09 with Sierra Halo (clinical diagnostics SaaS). They need an on-prem/VPC-capable inference integration for a triage assistant that must never leave PHI off-network. Primary ask: low-latency responses (<=300ms median for short prompts), model hallucination guardrails, and audit logs for each request. Likely candidate: Redwood Private with customer-managed control plane + Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable throughput.

Meeting notes (raw):
- Attendees: Claire Martin (Sierra Halo, Head of Platform), Dr. Evan Ruiz (clinical lead), Tomas Vega (infra), Aisha (Redwood SE) + Ben and Leila joined later.
- Use case: patient symptom triage -> short structured output (triage_code, urgency_level, recommended_next_steps). Outputs feed into their EHR via FHIR adapter.
- Data constraints: all identifiable patient text must remain in their VPC. They will provide streaming UDP telemetry to on-prem inference nodes for edge sites.
- Daily throughput: expected 20k requests/day peak; concurrency: bursts up to 400 RPS for short queries.
- Latency target: p50 <= 300ms, p95 <= 800ms for short chats (<=80 tokens out). Cost sensitivity moderate — willing to reserve capacity if it reduces cost predictability.
- Security/Compliance: HIPAA, SOC2 in roadmap. They already have a KMS (AWS KMS w/ dedicated CMK) and want HSM-ish assurances.
- Observability ask: per-request token cost, per-route latency, persistent audit trail (immutable).
- Failure mode: must fallback to a deterministic rules engine (on-device) when model is unavailable.

Core integration requirements (parsed):
1) Private deployment: control plane in Redwood, but all inference nodes in their VPC / on-prem. No patient text egress.
2) Dedicated capacity pool per region / site: predictable GPUs pinned to model family, autoscale policy with burst headroom up to 2x baseline.
3) Prompt templates: structured output schema enforcement (JSON schema) + function/tool calling to produce FHIR bundle.
4) Real-time audit logs sent to their SIEM (syslog/S3) with request id, model version, output hash.
5) KMS integration: customer key wrap for data at rest; per-tenant key.
6) Canary rollout path: need staged model rollouts (canary -> regional -> global) with rollback on quality regressions.
7) Redaction pipeline: optional client-side PII redaction before inference for non-PHI fields.
8) Offline deterministic fallback: local rules engine invoked if latency or confidence below threshold.

Gotchas / risks called out during call:
- Telemetry: they plan to stream patient transcripts from kiosks; UDP stream edge nodes may reorder messages — must ensure sequence handling before batching.
- KV cache: clinical prompts often reuse patient context (last visit). Must design prefix caching carefully to avoid leaking sensitive context across requests.
- Quantization: they want 8-bit model to save memory; we need to test hallucination/regression for their prompt set.
- Model vetting: clinical team insists on auditability of model outputs for any adverse event. Need clear provenance metadata (model_hash, tokenizer version, kernel flags).
- Network topology: some edge sites are air-gapped intermittently — we must support fully offline inference nodes and asynchronous sync of logs/metrics.
- FHIR mapping: mapping model JSON to FHIR claims must be validated with test-suite. Potential mismatch for severity enums.

Open questions to resolve (priority order):
- Q1: Will Sierra Halo provide an isolated subnet per clinical site or a single VPC peered to Redwood-managed subnets? (Impacts control plane connectivity design) — owner: Tomas Vega, due: 2026-03-17.
- Q2: Which models are acceptable (open-source families)? Do they require any specific model licensing vetting? (legal check) — owner: Claire, cc: Legal, due: 2026-03-18.
- Q3: Confirm retention policy for audit logs and whether patient identifiers must be hashed before shipping to Redwood control plane. (compliance) — owner: Aisha / security, due: 2026-03-16.
- Q4: Fallback rules engine spec: provide a list of deterministic rules and priority ordering for fallback. (integration) — owner: Dr. Evan, due: 2026-03-22.

Immediate next steps (action items):
- [Aisha] Draft high-level architecture diagram for Private + Dedicated + edge sync; attach to Confluence (CONF-2345) and send to Claire — due 2026-03-12. (DONE: initial draft v0.1)
- [Ben] Run quick regression tests on our 8-bit quantized variant for their short prompt set (use synthetic clinical prompts they shared) and record hallucination delta — due 2026-03-19.
- [Leila] Produce estimate for reserved capacity (GPU type: A10G vs A100) with cost/year and burst headroom options — due 2026-03-15.
- [Tom] Create onboarding checklist for customer KMS integration and HSM requirements; confirm what we can support in Private — due 2026-03-18.
- [Claire] Share sample FHIR mapping doc + test cases (CSV) — due 2026-03-16.

Suggested Redwood product mapping (quick):
- Redwood Private: control plane + customer-managed inference nodes (matches PHI constraint).
- Redwood Dedicated: reserved capacity pools for peak predictability and SLO enforcement.
- Console rollouts: use canary/A-B with automatic fallback policies and per-prompt evaluation hooks.
- Optimize: enable prefix caching and batching suggestions; but add strict tenant isolation for KV.
- Observability: enable token-level breakdown + export connectors to their SIEM.

Quick timeline (ballpark, rough):
- Week 0: contract/legal + scope sign-off (2–4 weeks for HIPAA addendum).
- Weeks 1–3: architecture design + test harness for clinical prompts + quantization regression tests.
- Weeks 4–8: Private deployment provisioning in their VPC + initial model onboarding + canary.
- Weeks 9–12: broad rollout, monitoring, and runbook handoff.

Notes-to-self / scratch ideas:
- We should prepare a small offline inference appliance pattern that can run FOSS weights with Redwood runtime in air-gapped mode (USB sync of metrics metadata).
- Consider shipping a small local LRU cache for patient prefix context that gets zeroed per-session to avoid cross-session leakage.
- Propose a model provenance header that includes 'model_hash:v1|quant:8bit|kernel:fast-attn' in every audit row.

Prompt engineering starter (for tests):
- System: "You are a clinical triage assistant. For the following patient note, output JSON with keys: triage_code, urgency_level (low/medium/high), recommended_next_steps (array), confidence_score (0-1). Do not produce any PHI other than tokens from the input. If you are unsure, return confidence_score < 0.4 and leave recommended_next_steps empty."
- Example patient note: "42F, cough x3d, temp 101.2F, O2 97%. No chest pain, mild wheeze."

Edge-case tests to build into harness: missing vitals, long history text with prior visits, multiple patient mentions (ensure single patient context is used), punctuation-heavy physician notes.

Other references: compare notes with prior similar engagement (see 'aurora-healthworks-shiftboard-kiosk-diary' for edge sync pattern), and reference the Dedicated sizing doc in /shared_drives/engineering/dedicated/capacity-estimates (link in CONF page).

Final thought: emphasis on auditability and offline mode; those are the gating items. Next sync scheduled 2026-03-17 at 9am PT (internal prep 8:15am PT).

--- raw call transcript snippets (copied for verbatim capture):
- Claire: "We cannot have any patient text leave our network, that's non-negotiable."
- Dr. Evan: "I need to be able to show provenance if something goes wrong — who, which model, which version."
- Tomas: "Some of our clinics are on flaky links — we'll need robust retry and offline queueing."

End of dossier.

(Keep this in users/ for working drafts — move to shared_drives when architecture is agreed.)
